issues.finding: The final clause says substitution is undefined when the bound variable equals the variable being replaced. The immediately following explanation correctly requires substitution of y for x in lambda-x.x to leave lambda-x.x unchanged.
issues.proposed_resolution: Add the matching-binder identity branch and reserve undefinedness for the remaining unsafe abstraction cases; keep the frozen source and existing labels unchanged.

issues.finding: The proof assumes x differs from the binder despite the matching-binder case, infers x not free in an undefined Q instead of the body P, and prints a duplicate equality in the displayed calculation.
issues.proposed_resolution: Handle the matching-binder identity separately; in the distinct-binder case derive x not free in P, and remove the duplicate display equality.

issues.finding: The statement has a stray parenthesis. The application step substitutes for y although the theorem substitutes for x. The abstraction premise switches x and y, and its set calculation removes the wrong variables, omits a closing delimiter, and invokes x not free in N where the definition requires y not free in N.
issues.proposed_resolution: Repair the statement, use x throughout the application step, derive x free in P from x free in lambda-y.P, and compute ((FV(P) minus x) union FV(N)) minus y using y not free in N.

issues.finding: The theorem asserts a reverse substitution equality without requiring that the reverse substitution be defined. For distinct x and y, M=lambda-x.x has the forward matching-binder identity defined, but the reverse substitution is undefined under the x binder. The abstraction proof also omits the matching-variable case and does not establish all binder restrictions.
issues.proposed_resolution: Condition the equality on both substitutions being defined, treat x=y as identity, and in the distinct case justify that an abstraction binder differs from x and y and that y is not free in its body.
